Again, as stated by Lush Justice in Mullins vs Treasurer of Survey, (1880) 5 QBD 170, at p-173-"When one finds a proviso to a section the natural presumption is that, but for the proviso, the enacting part of the section would have included the subject-matter of the proviso."
